sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Four production cycles reviewed against control-house environmental and utility logs

**Instrumentation:** Fixed active near-infrared reflectance cameras, portable active reflectance meter, leaf-temperature references, independent illuminance loggers, and isolated power-quality monitors

**Study boundary:** Three enclosed growth bays and one matched control bay within an otherwise ordinary horticultural complex.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Canopy response:** The three study bays showed a synchronized near-infrared reflectance change during seven unprogrammed overnight intervals. The control bay did not.

**Systems comparison:** Lighting, irrigation, ventilation, carbon-dioxide, and utility logs showed no common command or interruption at the onset times.

**Physical outcome:** Growth rate and harvest mass remained within the facility's ordinary production range; retained tissue samples showed no abnormality.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Shared sensor calibration, undocumented control-network traffic, thermal lag, and cultivar response remain plausible.

**Unresolved point:** Portable instruments confirmed five of the seven events after the fixed cameras were independently recalibrated. No external radiative source was identified.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Low-amplitude synchronized canopy response without a matched facility-control event

**Action:** Retain isolated logging and compare against future maintenance and cultivar changes. No production interruption is directed.

**Review status:** Active for passive comparison; formal review resumes after a new confirmed event, major controls revision, or cultivar change.

**Release limit:** Product, operator, and property identifiers are outside this archive copy.
